social_circle.name: Cristina Morales

demographics.occupation: pediatric dental hygienist at a group practice on Five Forks Trickum Rd.
demographics.location: Lilburn, GA (Rockbridge Rd. area, ~8 min from Maria)
demographics.education: Associate of Science in Dental Hygiene, Gwinnett Technical College (2012)

background.how_they_met: Grew up together in the Saint John Neumann parish; Cristina is the daughter of Doña Rosa, the church lady who pulled Maria into parish festival planning in 2013. The two became inseparable as young mothers in the parish youth ministry in the mid-2010s.
background.why_close: Same parish roots, same Mexican-American bicultural experience, compatible temperaments (Maria is the organizer, Cristina is the processor). Cristina set up the 2023 GoFundMe when Hector hurt his back. Both marched together at the 2020 Decatur BLM protest and both are book club members. Cristina is a little more politically progressive and regularly pushes Maria's thinking.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Mostly Spanglish texts, fast and casual; uses lowercase; heavy on voice notes when the story is long; laughing-crying emoji; calls Maria 'comadre' even though they are not technically compadres; will send a meme in the middle of a serious conversation to keep it breathable.

shared_activities: Monthly book club (4+ years)
Sunday 10 AM English Mass at Saint John Neumann (sometimes the 12:30 Spanish together)
Occasional folklórico practice drop-ins
Coffee walks on Maria's non-yoga mornings
Venting sessions at El Bodegón after grocery runs
recent_text_topics: Processing Maria's November 2024 election grief and the parish-parking-lot cry; Cristina checking in on her every few days for months.
Coordinating book club — whose turn to host, what wine to bring, venting that Dolores keeps insisting on re-reading House of the Spirits.
Back-and-forth about Lupita's cuticle-picking and whether to push for a therapist this summer; Cristina backing Maria up.
Cristina trying to talk Maria into finally retaking the driver's test; Maria deflecting with jokes.
Planning logistics for Maria's July folklórico performance at the Atlanta Latin American Festival (carpools, childcare overlap).
Cristina asking for Maria's pan de muerto recipe for her niece's Day of the Dead school project.

Q26, Q29: marched with Maria in Decatur June 2020. Q35: set up GoFundMe during Hector's back injury. Q44, Q45, Q49: primary emotional-support contact (post-election cry, spiraling, 'basically therapy').

social_circle.name: Esperanza Gutiérrez

demographics.occupation: semi-retired housecleaner (scaled back due to diabetes); occasional clients through Servicio Limpio (owner Paty) in Dunwoody/Sandy Springs
demographics.location: Lilburn, GA (off Killian Hill Rd., ~12 minutes from Maria)

background.how_they_met: Mother. Brought Maria from León, Guanajuato to the U.S. in 1996 when Maria was five.
background.why_close: Maria is the oldest of four and effectively co-parented her three younger siblings from age ten onward. After Esperanza's Type 2 diabetes and neuropathy worsened, Maria became her medical advocate — manages her glucose log, translates paperwork, cooks diabetic-friendly Sunday lunches, helps with Medicare forms. Esperanza is also Maria's day-to-day childcare backup (picks Mateo up when he's sick at school because Maria does not drive confidently).

interests: tending her small front-yard rose bed
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Spanish only, 90% voice notes because her eyes hurt looking at the screen. Sends lots of prayer-hands and flower stickers. Occasionally a suspicious WhatsApp forward about 'natural diabetes cures' that Maria has to gently debunk. Types in all caps when she does type.

shared_activities: Sunday 1 PM big family lunch at Esperanza's house (weekly)
Doctor appointments — Maria translates and takes notes at Esperanza's endocrinology visits
Grocery runs when Esperanza has a bad-feet day
Glucose-log review twice a week
Helping Mom navigate Medicare and utility paperwork
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (child-logistics texts + check-ins, mostly voice notes)
recent_text_topics: Daily glucose readings; Maria nagging her about eating pan dulce at breakfast again.
Coordinating Mateo pickup last Thursday when he had a stomachache at Camp Creek Middle — Esperanza picked him up because Maria was at the arts center.
Follow-up on Esperanza's most recent A1C result and whether Dr. Chen wants to adjust her metformin.
Planning Esperanza's birthday in December and the Posadas food lineup.
Esperanza forwarding a WhatsApp chain claiming cinnamon cures diabetes; Maria gently pasting the CDC en español link.
Asking Maria to translate a letter from the property tax office.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'My parents Ramon and Esperanza live about twelve minutes away off Killian Hill Road... my mom for child logistics. If Mateo has a stomachache at school, it's Mom who picks him up.' Q17: Maria helps her parents with English paperwork and Medicare. Q35: 'My mom's diabetes is the biggest ongoing thing... I manage her glucose log and cook diabetic-friendly food for Sundays.' Q42, Q46: mother's health hesitancy and depression context. Implied mother also on WhatsApp via Q42 ('tías' forwards).

social_circle.name: Adriana Gutiérrez-Ramírez

demographics.occupation: part-time medical billing clerk at a Duluth primary care office
demographics.education: high school diploma (Meadowcreek High, 2013); one year at Georgia State Perimeter before stopping

background.how_they_met: Sister. Maria helped raise her — was 'heating up tortillas, changing diapers, signing permission slips' from age ten (Q01).
background.why_close: Long-standing older-sister-as-second-mother dynamic. Three kids of her own means Adriana is the sibling most in the thick of the same parenting season as Maria. They trade kid hand-me-downs, coordinate cousin logistics, and run the family group chat together.

interests: reality TV (Love Is Blind, 90 Day Fiancé)
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Fast, heavy emoji, mixes Spanish and English mid-sentence. Sends lots of TikTok reels. Has a running private chat and a family group chat with Maria. Venting is about 60% of her texts; crisis energy about 20%; cute kid photos the rest.

shared_activities: Sunday 1 PM family lunch at Mom's (alternates hosting with Maria)
Cousin playdates on weekends — Adriana's three kids and Lupita/Mateo
Group chat 'Las Buendia-Gutiérrez' with Maria, Adriana, Javier, and Tomás
Quinceañera and birthday party planning (Adriana is Maria's second-in-command on big family events)
Swapping kid clothes Gaby has outgrown for Mateo's cleats rotation
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (mostly group chat, plus 1-on-1 several times a week)
recent_text_topics: Fallout of the November 2024 family-group-chat argument where two cousins admitted voting Trump — Adriana and Maria comparing notes on whom to still invite to Thanksgiving.
Planning Lupita's quinceañera (October 2027) — Adriana pitching in ideas at the $4,000 budget tier since she just navigated Gaby's October 2024 quince.
Her middle kid's IEP meeting next week — Adriana nervous, Maria offering to come translate.
Costco run coordination because Maria does not drive and Adriana has the SUV.
Mom's latest A1C panic — who will go to which appointment.
A running joke about Tío Roberto's latest dinner-table comment.

social_circle.name: Javier Gutiérrez

demographics.occupation: diesel mechanic at a heavy-truck repair shop near Buford
demographics.education: high school diploma; diesel technician certification from Lanier Technical College

background.how_they_met: Brother. Second of Maria's three younger siblings.
background.why_close: Quiet, dependable brother who shows love through practical help. Gave Maria and Hector the Ring doorbell for Christmas. Paid their electric bill unasked one month when Hector was laid up with his back injury in 2023. Lent Maria $300 for Thanksgiving 2024, repaid December 15. Often fixes Maria's and Hector's cars on the side.

key_traits: less churchy than the rest of the family
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short texts, no emoji, occasional thumbs-up. Prefers voice calls for anything real. Will text an inappropriate meme about Tío Roberto every few weeks to make Maria laugh. Responds to emotional topics with 'let me know if you need $' more than with words.

shared_activities: Sunday family lunch at Mom's (when not on a tow job)
Car-maintenance help for Maria and Hector — oil changes, brake pads, free labor
Family group chat 'Las Buendia-Gutiérrez'
Birthday barbecues he hosts at his place in Buford twice a year
recent_text_topics: Hector's truck making a new noise — Javier offered to look at it this Saturday.
Mom's foot ulcer follow-up appointment next month — Javier asking if he should drive her.
A check-in after Maria paid him back the $300 Thanksgiving loan in December — he sent a thumbs-up and a joke about charging interest.
Random meme about the family WhatsApp conspiracy forwards.
Asking Maria to send him photos of the Ring doorbell installation because Hector still hasn't set up the monthly subscription properly.
Confirming he's bringing carne asada to Mateo's 12th birthday in August.

social_circle.name: Keisha Mitchell

demographics.education: B.A. in Elementary Education, Georgia State University; M.Ed. in progress

background.how_they_met: Met at Camp Creek Elementary around 2020 when Mateo was in her homeroom class; Maria kept showing up for school events and they bonded over a shared Zora Neale Hurston paperback at a PTA meeting. Maria brought her into the book club later that year.
background.why_close: The book club's most politically engaged member and Maria's go-to for race-conscious conversations. Marched together in Decatur (June 2020 BLM) with Cristina. Has been patient and generous teaching the group through How to Be an Antiracist (2021), White Rage, and Caste. Their kids overlapped at Camp Creek, giving them ongoing parenting-of-Black-and-Brown-boys-in-Gwinnett common ground.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Full sentences, proper punctuation, teacher-brain. Uses fewer emoji than Cristina but will drop a crying-laugh at a good joke. Sends book recommendations with photos of the dust jacket. Slower replies on weekdays during school hours.

shared_activities: Monthly book club (4+ years)
Occasional Decatur bookstore (Charis Books) runs together
Mutual-aid coordination — Keisha helped Maria get Mateo paired with a good 5th-grade teacher the year she wasn't his homeroom
Check-ins after racial incidents (e.g., the bus n-word incident in December)
Supporting Black-owned Stone Mountain bakery together on weekends
recent_text_topics: Processing the December bus incident where a classmate called Mateo the n-word; Keisha both comforting Maria and coaching her on the school-meeting strategy with the principal.
Caste book progress — which chapter they're on, and whether to extend discussion to two months since it's heavy.
Exchanging reactions to school-board book-ban headlines out of Forsyth and Cobb counties.
Keisha asking Maria to translate a parent-teacher letter for a Spanish-speaking family in her class.
Checking whether Maria wants to co-host a voter-registration table at Camp Creek's fall festival again.
A running joke from book club about Dolores's fourth re-read of The House of the Spirits.
